graph.summary: Allopurinol → Xanthine dehydrogenase/oxidase → uric acid biosynthetic process → uric acid → Gout

evidence.snippet: Allopurinol and its active metabolite, oxypurinol, reduce uric acid concentrations through xanthine oxidase inhibition by suppressing the conversion of hypoxanthine and xanthine.
evidence.explanation: Pharmacokinetic review confirming that allopurinol acts by inhibiting xanthine oxidase (XDH/XO), thereby suppressing conversion of hypoxanthine and xanthine to uric acid.

paper.title: Population Pharmacokinetic Models of Oxypurinol in Adults: A Systematic Review.

evidence.snippet: Both Feb and ALP inhibited the upregulation of xanthine dehydrogenas/xanthine oxidase (XDH/XOD), UA levels, and UA transporters (URAT1 and GLUT9) induced by MSU, with Feb having a more pronounced effect.
evidence.explanation: In vitro study showing allopurinol (ALP) inhibits XDH/XOD activity and reduces uric acid (UA) levels in MSU-treated cells.

paper.title: Febuxostat alleviates gout-associated hyperuricemia and inflammation by downregulating IL1A to modulate TLR2/TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathway.

evidence.snippet: Xanthine dehydrogenase (XDH) is an enzyme that catalyzes the sequential conversion of hypoxanthine to xanthine, and of xanthine to urate.
evidence.explanation: XDH catalyzes the final two steps of uric acid biosynthesis (hypoxanthine→xanthine→urate), directly driving the uric acid biosynthetic process.

paper.title: Exploring the relationship between XDH gene variants and serum urate and xanthine dehydrogenase levels in gout.

evidence.snippet: Xanthine oxidase (XO), the rate-limiting enzyme in uric acid production, represents a core therapeutic target for gout.
evidence.explanation: XO/XDH is identified as the rate-limiting enzyme in uric acid production, confirming it positively regulates the uric acid biosynthetic process.

paper.title: Xanthine oxidase inhibitors for gout: Applications and novel drug development.

evidence.snippet: Xanthine dehydrogenase (XDH) is a key enzyme in urate biosynthesis, and genetic variations in its XDH gene can influence the amount or activity of the enzyme, as well as the levels of urate produced.
evidence.explanation: Urate biosynthesis driven by XDH produces uric acid (urate); increased XDH activity or expression correlates with higher urate levels, confirming the biosynthetic process increases uric acid abundance.

paper.title: Exploring the relationship between XDH gene variants and serum urate and xanthine dehydrogenase levels in gout.

evidence.snippet: Allopurinol and its active metabolite, oxypurinol, reduce uric acid concentrations through xanthine oxidase inhibition by suppressing the conversion of hypoxanthine and xanthine.
evidence.explanation: Blocking xanthine oxidase (the enzyme driving the uric acid biosynthetic process) reduces uric acid concentrations, confirming the biosynthetic process is the source of uric acid abundance.

paper.title: Population Pharmacokinetic Models of Oxypurinol in Adults: A Systematic Review.

evidence.snippet: Gout is an aseptic inflammatory disease caused by monosodium urate (MSU) crystal deposition.
evidence.explanation: Elevated uric acid (monosodium urate) leads to crystal deposition, the direct cause of gouty inflammation, confirming uric acid contributes to gout.

paper.title: Neutrophil extracellular traps in gout: from immune defense to pathological dynamic equilibrium.

evidence.snippet: Xanthine oxidase (XO), the rate-limiting enzyme in uric acid production, represents a core therapeutic target for gout.
evidence.explanation: Uric acid production (via XO) is the core driver of gout pathogenesis, confirming that uric acid contributes to gout.

paper.title: Xanthine oxidase inhibitors for gout: Applications and novel drug development.
